questions.q: A patient with primary ovarian failure has reduced circulating oestradiol. Which pituitary hormone is expected to rise because ovarian negative feedback has fallen?
questions.explain: Oestradiol and inhibin normally exert negative feedback on the hypothalamus and pituitary. Ovarian failure reduces this feedback, so gonadotropins—particularly FSH—rise.

questions.q: Which hormone released by Sertoli cells selectively suppresses pituitary FSH secretion?
questions.explain: Sertoli cells secrete inhibin B, which provides negative feedback on the anterior pituitary to reduce FSH secretion. Testosterone from Leydig cells provides broader negative feedback through the hypothalamic-pituitary axis.
